capitals.name: Gelgel
capitals.note: Infobox 'Gelgel (Gelgel period)'; Samprangan was the Majapahit-period seat and Klungkung that of the Nine Kingdoms. The page gives no year for the move to Gelgel; the span is the state's life. Coordinates approximate (Gelgel, near Klungkung).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's row. Infobox: 'Gelgel Kingdom from 1478 to 1661' after 'vassal of Majapahit from 1343 to 1478'. The page gives no area (only a map caption for the mid-16th-century maximum, 'from Blambangan to western Sumbawa'). CONFLICT: Cliopatria's Majapahit shape, and the Majapahit dossier (se-02-c), keep Bali inside Majapahit until 1518, so these cells overlap for 1478-1518 (42 of the 73 cells of the Balinese 1609 shape lie in the Majapahit 1516 shape); the colour agent or reviewer must choose.

7,719 km2 (25 cells): Bali island (24 cells of Natural Earth's Bali, 22 of them in the shape) plus three cells at Java's eastern tip (Banyuwangi coast, 114.3-114.8 E, 8.2-8.4 S) that the Blambangan page places in Blambangan. Corrected to the island. 'Gelgel reached its apogee during the reign of Dalem Baturenggong, as Lombok, western Sumbawa and Blambangan on easternmost Java, were united under Gelgel's suzerainty': the suzerainty is a tint (ledger), not in the shape. No infobox area.

union.text: western Lombok, round Mataram (the researcher's disc)

correction.text: Bali plus western Lombok, 35 cells, valid 1609-1682; Cliopatria's 22,062 km2 outline adds eastern Lombok and western Sumbawa (up to 117.9 E)

keyframe_review.note: The Lombok page: 'the neighbouring Balinese who took control of western Lombok in the early seventeenth century' and 'The Makassarese meanwhile invaded eastern Lombok from their colonies in neighbouring Sumbawa'; the Gowa page has the first Makassar attack on Sumbawa in 1618. So eastern Lombok and Sumbawa are not Bali's direct land in 1609-1682; they are the suzerainty tint of the ledger until 1618. The Bali page's mid-16th-century apogee (Lombok, western Sumbawa, Blambangan) is undated and the Lombok page has 'numerous competing and feuding petty states' under Sasak princes before the 17th century. Cliopatria's 1609 year matches the Lombok page's 'early seventeenth century'.

Verdict changes the shape and holds 1683-1686: Bali island only, as in Cliopatria (minus the three Java-edge cells). 'After 1651 the Gelgel kingdom began to break up due to internal conflicts'; 'In 1686 a new royal seat was established in Klungkung'. The Lombok page has the Balinese in western Lombok from the early 17th century and holding 'the whole island by 1750', so Cliopatria's loss of Lombok in 1683 is not supported by that page and is read as the break-up of Gelgel into the Nine Kingdoms (Karangasem and others), whose Lombok holdings belong to the 'bali' dossier.

ledger.note: 1478: the Gelgel kingdom of Bali begins after Majapahit's vassalage. Infobox: 'vassal of Majapahit from 1343 to 1478; Gelgel Kingdom from 1478 to 1661'. Dalem Ketut had founded a new royal seat at Gelgel while Samprangan lapsed.

notes: Cliopatria 'Balinese Kingdom' (3 shapes, 1519..1686) shares Wikipedia 'Bali Kingdom' and Wikidata Q12491027 with 'Early Balinese Kingdoms' (922-1343) and 'Bali' (1687-1907). They are different states here, as the Early Balinese dossier (se-02-a) already assumed: the Bali page itself divides the history into a sovereign kingdom to 1343, a Majapahit vassal phase 1343-1478, the Gelgel Kingdom (1478-1661, with a break-up after 1651) and the Nine Kingdoms from 1686; Cliopatria has no Bali shape between 1343 and 1518, so no single dossier can span them without a Majapahit gap. The colour agent may still choose to give the three rows one hue (all family southeast-asia). (1) Start 1478 comes from the infobox; Cliopatria starts 1519, and the new 1478-1518 keyframe overlaps Majapahit's shape (which keeps Bali to 1518). (2) The page's infobox puts Dalem Baturenggong at c. 1460-1550, which does not fit a Gelgel period beginning in 1478; the dossier uses the period dates. (3) The 1609 shape (22,062 km2) is cut to Bali plus western Lombok; eastern Lombok and western Sumbawa are carried as a tint 1519-1618 (confidence 1, the Bali page's undated 'apogee') and then pass to Makassar by the Gowa and Lombok pages. The Lombok page contradicts the Bali page on the pre-17th-century status of Lombok (petty Sasak states vs Gelgel suzerainty). (4) Cliopatria's 1683 loss of Lombok is not supported (Lombok page: Balinese on western Lombok throughout, all Lombok by 1750); the 'bali' dossier (another batch) should carry Karangasem and the other principalities' Lombok holdings. (5) The page's infobox ends the Gelgel period in 1661, the text has the break-up after 1651 and the Klungkung seat in 1686; 1686 is used (Cliopatria's last year). Counterparts without dossiers: the Sasak principalities of Lombok and the Sumbawa polities (the Gelgel tint 1519-1618 and the 1609 gain name them only as places). The fetch tool returns a model summary of each page; quotation marks mean 'as the fetched text gave it'. Page budget 1-2: Bali Kingdom and Lombok, with the Gowa and Blambangan pages already opened for neighbours.
